purpose: Adds a settings toggle (clientSideMimeTypeOverride/clientSideMimeTypes) that overrides WP 7.1+ core's client_side_supported_mime_types filter, and refactors encode-quality resolution to prefer core's size-aware wp_get_image_encode_quality() with flat wp_image_quality() and plugin-default fallbacks, fixing a latent (int) null-to-0 quality bug.
riskRationale: The MIME override is well-gated (function_exists + default-OFF) and the convert_image() refactor is an improvement, but routing the LQIP placeholder through core-quality resolution regresses LQIP encoding from the intended fixed quality 40 to core's flat JPEG quality (~82) on WP 6.7-7.0, silently inflating every base64 placeholder data URI on existing installs. No security concerns found.
breakingChanges: LQIP placeholder encoding quality changes from hardcoded 40 to core-derived quality on WP 6.7+, roughly doubling inline base64 placeholder payloads

client_side_supported_mime_types override (when enabled) replaces core's entire list without validating against what core/client worker can actually process, so unsupported formats selected in the UI are emitted as-is

text: The MIME-toggle work is clean, well-gated, and thoroughly tested, and routing convert_image() quality through a size-aware helper with a null-guarded flat fallback is a real improvement over the prior (int) null cast-to-0 bug. However, applying the same quality-resolution helper to generate_lqip() changes LQIP encoding from the deliberate fixed quality 40 to core's full JPEG quality (~82) on WP 6.7-7.0, silently inflating every placeholder data URI and contradicting the PR's own '(default still 40)' claim. The MIME override also replaces core's list unvalidated, and several minor defensive-coding gaps exist.

reasoning: LQIP thumbnails are intentionally low-quality placeholders; using core-quality resolution for them encodes at ~82 instead of 40 on WP 6.7-7.0, roughly doubling base64 placeholder size on every lazy-loaded image, which contradicts the PR's claim and harms the plugin's core performance goal. The MIME override's unvalidated list replacement should also be intersected with core's list before merge.

message: The client_side_supported_mime_types filter is correctly gated on both the core function existing (WP 7.1+) and the admin toggle being enabled, so older cores and default-OFF installs see zero behavior change. The callback also degrades gracefully to core's list when the stored value is empty/non-array.

resolve_encode_quality() is a solid layered fallback (size-aware helper → flat wp_image_quality() → plugin fallback) with all core calls function_exists()-gated, and it correctly eliminates the pre-existing bug where (int) wp_image_quality() cast null to 0.

Tests exercise the real private methods via reflection and correctly assert the flat-api fallback, the default fallback, and dimension forwarding to the size-aware helper, with explicit documentation of the Brain Monkey function-lifetime ordering constraint.

LQIP quality is no longer 40 as claimed. generate_lqip() now calls resolve_encode_quality('image/jpeg', 40, ...); on WP 6.7-7.0 the size-aware helper is absent, so it hits wp_image_quality('image/jpeg') which returns core's default JPEG quality (~82). The 20px~ thumbnail's inline base64 placeholder therefore encodes at ~82 instead of 40, roughly doubling the size of every placeholder data URI on existing WP 6.7-7.0 installs (and core's size-aware helper would return an even higher elevated quality for such tiny images on 7.1+). This directly contradicts the PR's '(default still 40)' claim and hurts the plugin's core performance goal. The size-aware helper is appropriate for convert_image() output, but placeholder size is intentional and core's per-MIME/per-size quality is meant for full images.
suggestion: Keep the fixed quality 40 for the LQIP encode instead of routing it through core-quality resolution; use resolve_encode_quality() only in convert_image().

message: filter_client_side_supported_mime_types() returns the sanitized/deduped selection verbatim, replacing core's entire list without any validation. The UI exposes HEIC/HEIF chips and the help text claims 'Formats core cannot process are ignored', but there is no enforcement — a selected format not supported by the client-side worker is emitted as-is and shadows core's authoritative list, which can cause uploads of that format to fail or silently lose client-side optimization.
suggestion: Validate the selection against what core reports it can support before replacing the list (intersect the selection with $supported_mime_types), and align the UI copy with the actual behavior.

message: The render path calls settings.clientSideMimeTypes.includes( option.value ) (lines 602 and 613) without an Array.isArray guard, unlike toggleClientSideMimeType() which guards defensively (line 114). If settings.clientSideMimeTypes is ever a non-array (e.g. a corrupted/stored string or a legacy wppoSettings.settings object missing the key), .includes would throw a TypeError and crash the tab, while the toggle handler treats that case as an empty selection.
suggestion: Guard the render access with a local list variable, e.g. const mimeList = Array.isArray( settings.clientSideMimeTypes ) ? settings.clientSideMimeTypes : []; then use mimeList.includes( option.value ) in both the chip className and checkbox checked logic.
suggestionCode:
const list = Array.isArray( settings.clientSideMimeTypes ) ? settings.clientSideMimeTypes : [];
// then: list.includes( option.value ) in className and checked

message: The default clientSideMimeTypes array (lines 44-50) is byte-for-byte identical to the DEFAULT_CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_TYPES constant (lines 87-93). The two will drift if core's default formats change, and the duplication is needless. Use the constant in the defaults so there is a single source of truth.
suggestion: Replace the inline literal at lines 44-50 with DEFAULT_CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_TYPES by hoisting the constant (and CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_OPTIONS) above defaultSettings, then referencing it in defaultSettings.

message: Silent no-op semantics: if the admin enables the override and unchecks every format chip, clientSideMimeTypes becomes empty and this callback returns core's default list unchanged (the graceful-degradation path). The UI copy says 'Unchecking a format makes the browser skip it', so unchecking all should disable client-side processing, but it instead restores core's full defaults — a confusing silent reversal of what the admin asked for.
suggestion: Differentiate 'override off' from 'override on with zero formats' — e.g. an empty selection when the override is enabled could return an empty list (disable browser processing) while keeping the core-list fallback only for the toggle-off case.

message: If wp_get_image_encode_quality() ever returns null (unsupported MIME or unexpected core behavior), the (int) cast coerces it to 0 — the same latent quality-0 bug the PR set out to eliminate, now reintroduced on the 7.1 path. The flat wp_image_quality() branch guards with a null !== check but the size-aware branch does not.
suggestion: Guard the 7.1 result before casting, mirroring the flat branch: $q = wp_get_image_encode_quality( $mime, $size, $fallback ); return null !== $q && $q > 0 ? (int) $q : $fallback;
